title: Habit Traction Lab — weekly scratchpad
content:
Week window: 2026-02-16 -> 2026-02-22
Context: personal traction exercises to protect deep work while shipping small but high-leverage infra changes (batching/caching config). Treating myself like a tiny product team: hypothesis -> experiment -> metric -> retro.

Objective (personal sprint): reclaim 8+ Deep Focus Hours (DFH) and complete 2 high-impact PRs that unblock model batching tests. Secondary: reduce distractions and build a 3-day streak of morning journaling.

North-star micro-metrics (short, simple):
- DFH (90+ minute uninterrupted blocks): target=8/week | actual=6.5 | delta=-1.5
- Context switches (work interruptions that break DFH): target<=4/day | actual=6.2 | delta=+2.2
- High-impact PRs merged: target=2 | actual=1 | blocked by infra flakes
- Morning journaling streak: target=3 days | actual=2
- Energy index (0..1 subjective): morning=0.8 | afternoon=0.5 | late=0.35

Why these metrics: DFH maps directly to shipping throughput for complex infra work; context switches are the biggest multiplier of cost. Morning journaling helps clarify daily intention and reduces friction to start deep work.

Current hypotheses to test (explicit):
H1: Consolidating low-value meetings to two clear slots (Tue/Thu) will add ~2 DFH/week.
H2: Moving non-blocking infra alerts to an async channel reduces context switches by 30%.
H3: 90/10 sprint rhythm (90 min work / 10 min reset) preserves energy vs 60/10 for longer tasks.

Mini experiment plan (this week):
- Experiment A: calendar curation. Action: move recurring syncs to Tue 2–4pm block; set DND 10–12 MWF. Measure DFH change and note subjective energy.
- Experiment B: alert routing. Action: convert one alert type (gpu-queue-high) to async webhook + summary at 11:00 instead of immediate pings. Track number of forced switches.
- Experiment C: sprint size. Action: 90-min deep sprints on PR work for model-batch-sim test; compare completion vs previous 60-min sprints.

Blocking items / signals to raise:
- Infra queue instability (Linear LNR-88) caused test flakiness; asks: can infra reserve a short CI slot to reproduce? (Raised to Priya, assigned to infra team)
- Calendar ownership: need buy-in from two recurring meeting attendees before consolidation.

Daily log snippets (quick, raw):
Mon 02/16: Forced to break DFH x2 for urgent infra alert. Energy 0.6 -> hit afternoon slump. Journaled for 8 minutes.
Tue 02/17: Moved 1:1 to Tue 10:00 — gained a 2-hour block in afternoon, started batching work on PR #458.
Wed 02/18: Successful 90-min sprint, made visible progress on test harness. Noticed attention drop after 75 mins; try 75/10 next time.
Thu 02/19: Alert routed to async channel; saw 1 forced switch less than baseline.
Fri 02/20: PR blocked by flaky GPU reservation — poke infra. Morning journaling streak broken (missed due to travel).

Quick retro (what worked / what didn't):
- Wins: DND blocks preserved single large block for PR work on Tue. Async alert routing reduced one immediate interruption on Thursday. 90-min sprint produced substantive test harness progress.
- Fails: still losing DFH to meeting creep and ad-hoc chat pings; morning journaling inconsistent when travel or early meetings happen. Infra flakes still kill momentum.

Concrete next actions (small, prioritized):
1) Follow up with infra on LNR-88 and request a short repro window (owner: Priya).
2) Add a calendar note for attendees explaining meeting consolidation + propose fixed Tuesday slot (owner: me).
3) Try 75/10 sprint next Wed and compare completion rate.
4) Automate morning journaling reminder at 08:30 local (10-min).
5) Capture two quick before/after screenshots of token-cost dashboard for batching experiment to quantify unit-economics tradeoff (very small, for motivation).

Ideas / backlog (brain-dump):
- Build a lightweight personal dashboard: small CSV with date, DFH, switches, PRs, journaling-streak to visualize trends. Could live in a private gist.
- Experiment: block one full day every 3 weeks as "no-meeting deep day" and measure delta in DFH over that week.
- Try pairing short retros (5 minutes) at end of day to capture wins before they fade.

Notes and links that mattered this week:
- Linear ticket: LNR-88 (infra/gpu-queue stability)
- Internal PR reference: github.com/redwood-inference/notes/pull/12 (scratch harness)
- Slack thread where meeting consolidation was discussed: slack thread C12345

Metrics snapshot (for quick copy into a tracker):
Date,DFH,Switches/day,PRs merged,Journaling-streak,Energy-morning
2026-02-16,1.5,6,0,0,0.7
2026-02-17,2.0,5,0,1,0.8
2026-02-18,1.5,6,0,1,0.85
2026-02-19,1.5,5,0,2,0.75
2026-02-20,0.0,8,1,2,0.45

One-liner to self: small wins compound — protect two 90+ minute blocks per week and remove the one noisy alert type.

Follow-ups for next check-in (2026-02-27):
- DFH >= 8? (yes/no)
- Did async alert reduce switches by >=20%?
- PRs merged = 2?
- Journaling streak >=3 days?

Random thought: treating productivity as an experiment reduces shame and focuses on measurement. Also, if infra can provide a dedicated short repro slot for heavy tests, the cadence of PRs could double.

Scratchpad end.
